1 --- 2 title: forbidden 3 description: API Reference for the forbidden function. 4 version: experimental 5 related: 6 links: 7 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden 8 --- 9 10 The `forbidden` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 403 error page. It's useful for handling authorization errors in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`forbidden.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden). 11 12 To start using `forbidden`, enable the experimental [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts) configuration option in your `next.config.js` file: 13 14 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 15 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 16 17 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 18 experimental: { 19 authInterrupts: true, 20 }, 21 } 22 23 export default nextConfig 24 ``` 25 26 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 27 module.exports = { 28 experimental: { 29 authInterrupts: true, 30 }, 31 } 32 ``` 33 34 `forbidden` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 35 36 ```tsx filename="app/auth/page.tsx" switcher 37 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 38 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 39 40 export default async function AdminPage() { 41 const session = await verifySession() 42 43 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 44 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 45 forbidden() 46 } 47 48 // Render the admin page for authorized users 49 return <> 50 } 51 ``` 52 53 ```jsx filename="app/auth/page.js" switcher 54 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 55 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 56 57 export default async function AdminPage() { 58 const session = await verifySession() 59 60 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 61 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 62 forbidden() 63 } 64 65 // Render the admin page for authorized users 66 return <> 67 } 68 ``` 69 70 ## Good to know 71 72 - The `forbidden` function cannot be called in the [root layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout). 73 74 ## Examples 75 76 ### Role-based route protection 77 78 You can use `forbidden` to restrict access to certain routes based on user roles. This ensures that users who are authenticated but lack the required permissions cannot access the route. 79 80 ```tsx filename="app/admin/page.tsx" switcher 81 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 82 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 83 84 export default async function AdminPage() { 85 const session = await verifySession() 86 87 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 88 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 89 forbidden() 90 } 91 92 // Render the admin page for authorized users 93 return ( 94

The `@/*` path alias is configured correctly. Done.

Changes:
- `next.config.ts:3-5` — enabled experimental `authInterrupts` (required for `forbidden()`).
- `app/admin/page.tsx` — server component that calls `verifyAdmin()` and invokes `forbidden()` for non-admins.
- `app/forbidden.tsx` — custom 403 UI; Next.js returns the proper HTTP 403 status with this file convention.

Since `app/lib/auth.ts` currently returns a `user` role, visiting `/admin` will trigger `forbidden()` and render the 403 page. Change the mock session to `role: 'admin'` to see the dashboard.
